solution:
## Write 1200 in the form a × 10ⁿ
Move the decimal point so that $1 \le a < 10$: three places, so $n = 3$.
1200 &= 1.2 \times 10^3
## Write 0.27 in the form a × 10ⁿ
Move the decimal point one place right to get $2.7$, so $n = -1$.
0.27 &= 2.7 \times 10^{-1}
ANSWER: 1.2 \times 10^3, \quad 2.7 \times 10^{-1}

## Find where m(x) = 0
$m(x) = 0$ where the graph of $m$ meets the $x$-axis.
m(x) = 0 \text{ at } x &= 1
\text{and } x &= 4.5
## Find where the two graphs cross
The graphs of $k$ and $m$ cross at $x = 2$ and $x = 3.5$.
## Find where k(x) is less than m(x)
Between $x = 2$ and $x = 3.5$ the graph of $m$ is above the graph of $k$.
Outside that range, $m$ is below $k$. Do not include the endpoints, because there $k(x) = m(x)$.
k(x) < m(x) \text{ for } 2 &< x < 3.5
ANSWER: x = 1 \text{ or } x = 4.5; \quad 2 < x < 3.5

## Multiply out the bracket
-254 + (n-1)(4) &> 0
-254 + 4n - 4 &> 0
4n - 258 &> 0
## Isolate n
4n &> 258
n &> 64.5
## n must be a whole number
The smallest whole number greater than $64.5$ is $65$.
n &= 65
ANSWER: n = 65

## Simplify the bracket
\frac{n}{2}[2(-254) + 4n - 4] &= 0
\frac{n}{2}[-508 + 4n - 4] &= 0
\frac{n}{2}[4n - 512] &= 0
## Set the second factor to zero
A product is zero when a factor is zero. Since $n \neq 0$, the bracket must be $0$.
4n - 512 &= 0
## Solve for n
4n &= 512
n &= 128
ANSWER: n = 128

## Read the coordinates as (time, heart-rate)
The first co-ordinate is the time in minutes since the start, and the second is the heart-rate in BPM.
So $\mathbf{A}(6, 169)$ means that 6 minutes after the start, Joseph's heart-rate is 169 BPM.
ANSWER: \text{6 minutes after the start, his heart-rate is 169 BPM}

## Stays at the same level for 2 minutes
From $x = 6$ to $x = 8$ the heart-rate stays at 169, so draw a horizontal line to $(8, 169)$.
## Decreases by 10 BPM each minute for 2 minutes
\text{Drop} &= 10 \times 2
&= 20
\text{Heart-rate at } x = 10 &= 169 - 20
&= 149
## Draw the second line
Draw a straight line from $(8, 169)$ down to $(10, 149)$.
ANSWER: (6,169) \to (8,169) \to (10,149)

## Use h(6) = 169 from the table or graph
$c(x) = 0.1\,h(x) - 7$, and $h(6) = 169$.
## Substitute into c(x)
c(6) &= 0.1(169) - 7
&= 16.9 - 7
&= 9.9
ANSWER: 9.9 \text{ calories per minute}

## Find the length of the session
From 2:55 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. is 5 minutes, then 23 more minutes.
5 + 23 &= 28
## Find the beeps per minute
60 \div 15 &= 4
## Find the number of gaps between beeps
4 \times 28 &= 112
## Add the first beep
There is one more beep than there are gaps.
112 + 1 &= 113
ANSWER: 113 \text{ beeps}

## Identify a, b and c
$-1.14x^2 + 5.2x - 0.13 = 0$, so $a = -1.14$, $b = 5.2$, $c = -0.13$.
## Substitute into the quadratic formula
x &= \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}
x &= \frac{-5.2 \pm \sqrt{5.2^2 - 4(-1.14)(-0.13)}}{2(-1.14)}
## Evaluate the number under the square root
5.2^2 - 4(-1.14)(-0.13) &= 27.04 - 0.5928
&= 26.4472
## Work out both solutions
x &= \frac{-5.2 + \sqrt{26.4472}}{-2.28}
&\approx 0.025
x &= \frac{-5.2 - \sqrt{26.4472}}{-2.28}
&\approx 4.536
## Choose the maximum
$x = 0.025$ is the minimum at the start (the heart-rate dips slightly), so the maximum is at the other solution.
x &\approx 4.54
ANSWER: x = 4.54 \text{ minutes}

## Find 12% of 200 ml
\frac{12}{100} \times 200 &= 24
&= 24
ANSWER: 24 \text{ ml}

## Acid from Bottle A
From part (i), 200 ml from Bottle A contains 24 ml of acid.
## Acid from Bottle B
5\% \text{ of } 300 &= 0.05 \times 300
&= 15
## Total acid in the mixture
24 + 15 &= 39
## Total volume of the mixture
200 + 300 &= 500
## Concentration = acid ÷ total volume × 100
\frac{39}{500} \times 100 &= 7.8
&= 7.8
ANSWER: 7.8\%

## Compare 4% with the two bottles
Any mixture of the two bottles has a concentration between $5\%$ (all Bottle B) and $12\%$ (all Bottle A).
$4\%$ is below $5\%$, so it cannot be made.
ANSWER: \text{Mixtures can only be between } 5\% \text{ and } 12\%

## Percentage error = error ÷ intended value × 100
\text{Error} &= 260 - 250
&= 10
## Divide by the intended amount and multiply by 100
\frac{10}{250} \times 100 &= 4
&= 4
ANSWER: 4\%

## Count the corners and faces of a cube
A cube has 8 corners and 6 faces, so $C = 8$ and $F = 6$.
## Check the identity
C - E + F &= 8 - 12 + 6
&= -4 + 6
&= 2
ANSWER: C = 8,\ F = 6,\ \text{and } 8 - 12 + 6 = 2

## Substitute C and E into the identity
12 - 30 + F &= 2
-18 + F &= 2
## Solve for F
F &= 2 + 18
F &= 20
## Surface area = faces × area of one face
\text{Surface area} &= 20 \times 5
&= 100
ANSWER: 100 \text{ cm}^2

## Multiply every term by 6 to clear the fractions
\frac{6h+5p}{3} - \frac{6h+5p}{2} + h + p &= 2
2(6h+5p) - 3(6h+5p) + 6h + 6p &= 12
## Multiply out the brackets
12h + 10p - 18h - 15p + 6h + 6p &= 12
## Collect like terms
(12h - 18h + 6h) + (10p - 15p + 6p) &= 12
0h + p &= 12
p &= 12
ANSWER: p = 12

## Read the values from the graph
At $t = 0$ the graph is at 30 000. At $t = 1$ it is at 24 000.
V(0) &= 30\,000
V(1) &= 24\,000
ANSWER: V(0) = \text{€}30\,000,\ V(1) = \text{€}24\,000

## Find the fall in value in year 1
30\,000 - 24\,000 &= 6000
## Write the fall as a percentage of the starting value
\text{Percentage fall} &= \frac{6000}{30\,000} \times 100
&= 20
ANSWER: 20\%

## Turn the 20% fall into a multiplier
A fall of $20\%$ leaves $80\%$ of the value, so each year the value is multiplied by $0.8$.
## Multiply by 0.8 once for each year
V(1) &= 30\,000 \times 0.8
V(2) &= 30\,000 \times 0.8 \times 0.8
V(t) &= 30\,000(0.8)^t
ANSWER: V(t) = 30\,000(0.8)^t

## Substitute t = 4
V(4) &= 30\,000(0.8)^4
## Work out the power of 0.8
&= 30\,000(0.4096)
## Multiply
&= 12\,288
ANSWER: \text{€}12\,288

## Plot the two given points
At $t = 0$ the value is 30 000 and at $t = 1$ it is 24 000.
Draw a straight line through $(0, 30\,000)$ and $(1, 24\,000)$.
## Find the fixed fall each year
30\,000 - 24\,000 &= 6000
## Find when the value reaches 0
The value falls by 6000 each year, so the line meets the horizontal axis when the total fall is 30 000.
T &= \frac{30\,000}{6000}
&= 5
## Mark the point on the axis
The line reaches the horizontal axis at $(5, 0)$.
ANSWER: T = 5 \text{ years}

## Find the 30% deposit
0.3 \times 19\,445 &= 5833.5
## Find the total of the 36 monthly repayments
3 years is $3 \times 12 = 36$ months.
36 \times 206.97 &= 7450.92
## Add the deposit, the repayments and the lump sum
5833.5 + 7450.92 + 7389 &= 20\,673.42
ANSWER: \text{€}20\,673.42

## Usual time = distance ÷ speed
\frac{12}{60} &= 0.2
&= \frac{1}{5}
## Time with roadworks
\frac{12}{40} &= 0.3
&= \frac{3}{10}
## Percentage increase = increase ÷ original × 100
\frac{0.3 - 0.2}{0.2} \times 100 &= \frac{0.1}{0.2} \times 100
&= 50
ANSWER: 50\%

## Set the height equal to 3.2
-2t^2 + 5t + 1.2 &= 3.2
## Rearrange so one side is 0
-2t^2 + 5t - 2 &= 0
2t^2 - 5t + 2 &= 0
## Factorise and solve
(2t-1)(t-2) &= 0
t &= \tfrac{1}{2} \text{ or } t = 2
## Pick the time when the ball is falling
$t = \tfrac{1}{2}$ is before the highest point (at $t = 1.25$), so the ball is still rising. The ball is decreasing at $t = 2$.
ANSWER: t = 2 \text{ seconds}

## Differentiate h
\frac{dh}{dt} &= -4t + 5
## Greatest height: set the derivative to 0
-4t + 5 &= 0
-4t &= -5
t &= \frac{5}{4}
t &= 1.25
ANSWER: t = 1.25 \text{ seconds}

## Point where Keith hits the ball
At $t = 0$ the height is 1 metre, so $(0, 1)$ is on the graph.
## Greatest height
The greatest height is 5 m after 2 s, so the turning point $(2, 5)$ is on the graph.
## Use symmetry
A quadratic is symmetrical about its turning point, at $t = 2$. The point $(0, 1)$ is 2 to the left, so the point 2 to the right is $(4, 1)$.
## Draw the graph
Plot $(0, 1)$, $(2, 5)$ and $(4, 1)$. Draw a smooth, upside-down U-shaped curve through them, and continue it until it meets the horizontal axis a little after $t = 4$.
ANSWER: (0, 1),\ (2, 5),\ (4, 1)

## After a 15% discount, Keith pays 85%
100\% - 15\% &= 85\%
## Find 85% of €33
33 \times 0.85 &= 28.05
ANSWER: \text{€}28.05

## €49.50 is 123% of the price without VAT
The price without VAT is $100\%$, so with VAT it is $123\%$.
## Find 1%
1\% &= \frac{49.50}{123}
## VAT is 23%, so multiply by 23
\text{VAT} &= \frac{49.50}{123} \times 23
&\approx 9.26
ANSWER: \text{€}9.26

## Find L using the symmetry about the y-axis
$L$ is the reflection of $M(9, 1)$ in the $y$-axis, so $L = (-9, 1)$.
## (i) Find the length of LM
$L$ and $M$ have the same $y$-value, so the length is the difference in $x$-values.
|LM| &= 9 - (-9)
&= 18
## (ii) Write the equation of LM
Every point on $LM$ has $y = 1$, so the horizontal line is $y = 1$.
ANSWER: |LM| = 18, \quad y = 1

## N lies on the y-axis, so x = 0
Substitute $x = 0$ into $x + 4y - 13 = 0$.
0 + 4y - 13 &= 0
## Solve for y
4y &= 13
y &= \frac{13}{4}
## Write N as a pair of coordinates
$x = 0$ and $y = \frac{13}{4}$.
ANSWER: N = \left(0, \frac{13}{4}\right)

## Compare with the circle equation
A circle with centre $(h, k)$ and radius $r$ has equation $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$.
(x - 4)^2 + (y + 2)^2 &= 169
(x - 4)^2 + (y - (-2))^2 &= 13^2
## Read off the centre and radius
$h = 4$ and $k = -2$, so the centre is $(4, -2)$.
r &= \sqrt{169}
&= 13
ANSWER: \text{Centre} = (4, -2), \quad \text{Radius} = 13

## Substitute (11, 10) into the left-hand side
A point is on, inside or outside the circle depending on whether the left side equals, is less than, or is greater than $169$.
&(11 - 4)^2 + (10 + 2)^2
&= 7^2 + 12^2
&= 49 + 144
&= 193
## Compare with 169 and tick the box
$193 > 169$, so the point is outside the circle.
Tick the box: (11, 10) is outside k.
ANSWER: (11, 10) \text{ is outside } k

## Find the translation from (12, 11) to the centre
(22 - 12,\ 13 - 11) &= (10, 2)
## Apply the same translation again
The point $(12, 11)$ is on $s$, so the point on the other side of the centre, the same distance away, is also on $s$.
(22 + 10,\ 13 + 2) &= (32, 15)
ANSWER: (32, 15) \text{ (any valid point)}

## Find the translation from the centre of s to the touching point
The centres and the touching point are on one straight line, with the touching point between them.
(12 - 22,\ 11 - 13) &= (-10, -2)
## Halve it, since t has half the radius
\tfrac{1}{2}(-10, -2) &= (-5, -1)
## Move from the touching point by this amount
The centre of $t$ is this far from $(12, 11)$, continuing in the same direction.
(12 - 5,\ 11 - 1) &= (7, 10)
ANSWER: \text{Centre of } t = (7, 10)

## Put the numbers in order
$8,\ 8,\ 9,\ 11,\ 14,\ 17,\ 28$
## Pick the middle number
There are 7 numbers, so the median is the 4th number, which is $11$.
ANSWER: 11

## Use the median of 8 numbers
With 8 numbers the median is the average of the 4th and 5th numbers.
The new 4th and 5th numbers are the new number $x$ and $11$, so the median is their average.
\frac{x + 11}{2} &= 10.5
## Solve for x
x + 11 &= 21
x &= 10
ANSWER: 10

## Multiply the number of choices in each group
Ben picks one subject from each group, so the choices multiply.
3 \times 4 \times 5 &= 60
ANSWER: 60

## Extra subject added to Group A
4 \times 4 \times 5 &= 80
## Extra subject added to Group B
3 \times 5 \times 5 &= 75
## Extra subject added to Group C
3 \times 4 \times 6 &= 72
## Compare the three totals
$80 > 75 > 72$, so the largest number of choices comes from adding the subject to Group A.
ANSWER: \text{Group A}

## Find the total number of students
8 + 12 + 39 + 13 &= 72
## Find the angle for one student
A full circle is $360^\circ$, shared between 72 students.
\frac{360}{72} &= 5
Check: Distinction has $8 \times 5 = 40^\circ$, which matches the given sector.
## Find the angle for each other grade
\text{High Merit: } 12 \times 5 &= 60
\text{Merit: } 39 \times 5 &= 195
\text{Achieved: } 13 \times 5 &= 65
## Check the angles add to 360
40 + 60 + 195 + 65 &= 360
## Draw and label the sectors
Starting from the $40^\circ$ Distinction sector, measure $60^\circ$ anticlockwise for High Merit, then $65^\circ$ for Achieved. The rest of the circle is Merit, $195^\circ$.
ANSWER: \text{Distinction } 40^\circ,\ \text{High Merit } 60^\circ,\ \text{Merit } 195^\circ,\ \text{Achieved } 65^\circ

## (i) Write 80 and 120 in terms of the mean and standard deviation
100 - 20 &= 80
100 + 20 &= 120
So 80 to 120 is within 1 standard deviation of the mean.
## (i) Apply the empirical rule
The empirical rule says about $68\%$ of values are within 1 standard deviation of the mean.
$68\%$ of the people scored between 80 and 120.
## (ii) Use the 95% rule to find the top 2.5%
$95\%$ of values are within 2 standard deviations, so $5\%$ lie outside.
That $5\%$ is split evenly, so the top $2.5\%$ are more than 2 standard deviations above the mean.
## (ii) Find the least score
100 + 2(20) &= 100 + 40
&= 140
ANSWER: \text{(i) } 68\%, \quad \text{(ii) } 140
